title: Six Threads Under One Leaking Vault: Clones, Ledgers, Skinny T, the Stolen Volume, and Wario's Feywild Clause
subtitle: Cross-checking the two songs, the Treasury of Wonders loop, the week's three hauntings, and the two documents Wario has now called 'the Contract of Accord'.
summary: A custody, financial, and cross-filing reading of 'The Archive Hall and the Song "Alone"' (3 Aethel, 1035 BF), connecting the six-name clone sheet, the unguarded Archive Hall ledger substitution, Mr. T's match to Paulo's 'skinny T' line, the physical book removed by Beta Luigi, and Wario's corridor disclosure regarding Feywild contracts.
thesis: Beneath its chaotic surface, that late-night convergence on 3 Aethel inside the Archive Hall locks four separate threads of the 1035 BF Mario arc into a single room: inside financial tampering against Wario's Enterprise and the Treasury of Wonders, an unguarded archive vault directly adjoining Star Hill's clinic corridors, physical-world spillover across three hauntings in seven days culminating in Beta Luigi removing an actual book from the shelves, and Wario admitting under pressure that his 'Contract of Accord' binds him under Feywild terms where failure leaves 'no coming back — not for anyone.'

sections.heading: 1. The Accidental Headcount Inside the 'Wawario' Song Sheet
sections.sourceAnchor: Beat I–II — 'Nintendo, please make this into a reality of how many evil clones are there and if there is any more than we already know, please let us know.'
sections.body:
Taken at face value, the transcribed sheet Mr. T hands across the oak table reads like garbled street ephemera: misstated family ties, invented composite names ('Wario Bowser', 'Wart Bowser', 'Wawario'), and Mr. T's follow-up prompt adding 'Wawaluigi' with two prefixes. Cross-checked against the wider 1035 BF docket, however, its central obsession — proliferated doubles and uncounted variants — lands straight on top of active field sightings.

Within the surrounding sequence of filings, witnesses have already recorded Promo Mario operating as a composed studio double, GB Mario walking a gold road in greyscale proportions, three simultaneous copies of Mr. L standing outside Dr. Toad's Star Hill Clinic while the clinic's inpatient Luigi remains bedridden inside, and now Beta Luigi entering the adjacent Archive Hall with distinct attire, distinct memories of King Boo's chasm, and physical hands capable of lifting archive property. Waluigi blacking out his own name on the sheet reads first as wounded pride, yet it registers an exact boundary claim in a week where nearly every principal except Waluigi is splitting into versions.

sections.heading: 2. How the Ledger Tampering Works — and What the Open Shelf Proves
sections.sourceAnchor: Beats III–IV — Column 7 vs. Column 9 (~10,000 gp), backdated deposit (-14 days), Treasury of Wonders 5,000 gp withdrawal/re-deposit, and 'AUDIT REQUIRED - WARIO'.
sections.body:
Three separate facts establish that the financial tampering uncovered on 3 Aethel is an inside substitution rather than simple sloppy bookkeeping. First, the morning schedules delivered to Wario contain three distinct alterations pointing in the same direction: an approximate 10,000-gold spread between columns seven and nine, a quarterly client deposit stamped roughly two weeks before the underlying transaction occurred, and a 5,000-gold withdrawal from the Treasury of Wonders followed one month later by an equal re-deposit.

Second, when Mr. T reaches onto the Archive Hall shelves at random, both volumes of *The Complete Ledger of Wario's Enterprise* sit completely intact in plain reach, allowing immediate line-by-line proof that the circulating packet had been altered while master backups stayed untouched. Third, both Waluigi and Mr. T independently confirm that a facility supposed to carry round-the-clock guards has stood unstaffed for months — while Wario himself carries a brass key to its locked filing cabinets. Whoever altered those schedules knew nobody was watching the door, knew Wario would panic rather than notify the Toad Police Force over anything touching the Treasury of Wonders, and counted on Wario ignoring bottom-margin notes on his own daily reports.

sections.heading: 3. Identifying 'Skinny T' Across Adjacent Star Hill Nights
sections.sourceAnchor: Beat VII & The Rot-Zone at Star Hill (2 Aethel, 1035 BF) — Paulo's 'skinny T' line matched against Wario's corridor description of Mr. T.
sections.body:
One lingering loose end from the previous night's Star Hill crash (*The Rot-Zone at Star Hill*, 2 Aethel, 1035 BF) receives its cleanest candidate match here without either speaker realizing it. Outside Dr. Toad's clinic in the dark, syndicate courier Paulo mistook the tall silhouette of Mr. L for someone he knew from courier circles, remarking that he did not know 'skinny T' wore green.

Twenty-four hours later, inside the Archive Hall connected to that exact Star Hill clinic complex, we meet a gaunt, exhausted courier-auditor addressed exclusively as **Mr. T** — whom Wario explicitly describes in the corridor as a courier who knows far too much about gambling debts and dirty laundry. Same district, same overnight courier underworld, matching initial, and matching build: until a second courier using the single initial 'T' appears on the hill, Mr. T stands on the board as the primary match for Paulo's street reference.

sections.heading: 4. Three Hauntings in One Week — Crossing from Apparition to Solid Theft
sections.sourceAnchor: Beats V–VI — First a Boo, second a giant moth, third Beta Luigi crushing a live Fire Flower and removing one bound shelf volume.
sections.body:
Wario's whispered outburst behind the bookcase turns what would look like an isolated haunting into an escalating seven-day pattern inside the same room: first a Boo apparition, second a giant moth entity the week prior, and third Beta Luigi's arrival during the thunderstorm on 3 Aethel — immediately preceding Wario's unguarded reference to a 'Feywild breach.' Note also the physical precursor twenty minutes earlier: rainwater seeping straight through uncracked vault stone directly above the reading table.

Crucially, Haunting #3 crosses the line separating vision from physical presence twice in front of three witnesses. Beta Luigi carries a live, powered Fire Flower into the room and crushes its petals flat under his boot on the stone floor; then, after the spectral chorus, the unseen barrier, the fifteen-foot crimson ghost, and Mario's disembodied voice all cut off together, Beta Luigi stands up, reaches onto a physical oak bookcase, pulls down one bound volume, and walks out the door holding it. Whatever entered the Archive Hall left missing inventory behind.

sections.heading: 5. Two Opposite Luigi Songs on Consecutive Star Hill Nights
sections.sourceAnchor: Beat VI ('Alone' & Italian lines) contrasted against Mr. L's lava-bridge verses in 'The Rot-Zone at Star Hill' (2 Aethel, 1035 BF).
sections.body:
Placing 2 Aethel and 3 Aethel side by side exposes a stark symmetry across Star Hill. Outside the clinic on 2 Aethel, Mr. L sang calmly in three bodies about hating his brother, burning the bridge, and watching Mario drown below while smiling. Inside the connected Archive Hall on 3 Aethel, Beta Luigi collapsed on the stone singing the exact emotional inverse: unbearable self-hatred for cowering at King Boo's chasm when Mario needed him most.

Equally striking is the Italian exchange answering him out of empty air: absolution first (*Ti perdono. Vai avanti*), delegation second (*Tocca a te salvarli*), explicit finality third (*Mario non c'è più — non farmi morire invano*), and identity restoration fourth (*Mostra loro che sei il fratello di Mario! Sei Luigi!*). Yet Beta Luigi's final murmured line twists that charge back toward isolation — vowing to make them atone *alone* before taking a shelf book and walking out without speaking a word to Wario or Waluigi.

sections.heading: 6. Two Contracts Under One Name: What Is Inside Wario's Coat Pocket?
sections.sourceAnchor: Beat VII — Wario rejecting gold ('Gold doesn't bring dead people back!') and naming the parchment one of 'these Feywild contracts.'
sections.body:
Across three consecutive 1035 BF filings, Wario has applied the exact title *Contract of Accord* to documents that behave completely differently. At the Debt Siege on 30 Harvestide, Wario used that name for a written forty-percent partnership contract signed over Waluigi's name; on the Star Hill roof on 2 Aethel, he negotiated it upward to sixty-thirty over Waluigi's working notebook. Yet inside the Archive Hall corridor on 3 Aethel, clutching a bent, torn parchment he would not let anyone read, Wario strikes solid stone, rejects gold reward money outright, warns that failure leaves no coming back for anyone, and demands that Mr. T explain how *Feywild contracts* operate.

Either Wario has reused his favorite legal-sounding title to disguise a genuine Feywild pact binding him to the breach crisis, or the original Accord carries supernatural enforcement clauses Wario concealed from Waluigi from day one. Either way, when Wario waves away gold with "gold cannot restore the dead!", the coercion on him is mortal, not commercial.
